summary.name: SRE: An incomplete guide to cultural Narnia
summary.one_liner: A 2016 blog post by Anthony Caiafa giving opinions on how to structure and culturally introduce Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams inside a company.
use_cases: Deciding how to structure an SRE organization
Explaining SRE to colleagues or management
Choosing between embedded and centralized SRE teams
Planning SRE responsibilities and on-call duties
Onboarding junior operations staff through frontline support
summary.what_it_does: The page is an opinion essay, not a software tool. It defines SRE as a mix of operations, development and infrastructure skills plus a cultural mindset rather than only tooling. It lists areas of responsibility such as monitoring, configuration management, data warehousing, capacity planning, documentation and incident response. It compares Application SRE (embedded in service teams, roughly 70% time to that team) with Infrastructure SRE (building core infrastructure and tools for others). It recommends a centralized reporting chain and an optional frontline support tier for handling alerts and runbooks.
notable: Splits SRE into Application SRE (embedded in service teams) and Infrastructure SRE (core platform and tooling)
Argues for a centralized reporting chain even when SRE work is split across teams
Suggests an optional frontline support tier that handles first-wave pages and follows runbooks
Author states there is no single formula and warns against adopting SRE just because it is a trend
caveats: Author states these are personal opinions and experience, not a prescribed model
Mostly high-level; the author says much more information is left out of the post
